patch.value: The release gate classifies production errors by message prose and reads none of the 236 error codes the product declares, so every waiver is a latent re-block and a broad substring is a silent waiver

The gate that decides whether production errors block a release partitions Sentry issues by lowercased message substring. It carries 34 hand-written patterns across four lists (8 console, 23 CLI, 1 validation, 2 environment) and references none of the 236 stable error codes the product declares, even though the handled-error channel already ships pm.error_code to Sentry as a tag and every refusal envelope carries a code and a urn:pm-cli:error type. Two failure modes follow and both are already realized in this repository. Latent re-block: message text is under no contract, so any wording change silently unmatches its pattern and re-blocks a cut; the file's own comments record that a per-count list re-blocked a release once a new count appeared, and the repair was to loosen the prose rather than to bind to a code. Silent over-waiver: broad substrings such as structural error(s) and item(s) failed to apply waive any future unrelated exception whose message happens to contain them, and no check asserts that a pattern still matches something or that it matches only what it intends. The asymmetry is inverted today: the release contract spec pins the allowlist pattern strings, so the waiver list is frozen while the messages it must match are free.

The release error classifier decides from the declared error code and exit code, not from message text, for every family it waives; A check fails when a waiver entry matches nothing in the window, so a dead waiver cannot silently persist; A check fails when a waiver entry matches an error family it was not declared for, proving the waiver is not broader than its intent; Error messages become free to reword without touching the release gate, and a negative control proves a rewording no longer re-blocks a cut
